P1.evidence: No setter suffix on the title and no setter named on the call, so the read-back check does not apply. Frame was the usual abbreviated two parts — 'where are you today? Where do you want to be? we can help, I can show you one of the many options that we have. Okay?' — missing 'what's in the way' and 'what you need'. Agreement was a single 'Sure'. Open question ran cleanly: 'So I'll leave the floor over to yourself. How can we potentially help you?'

P2.evidence: Age was asked, but not until 00:18:50 and only as a setup for the identity question. Height and current weight were never asked at all — the only numbers on record are historical (187 lb out of basic, close to 230 lb leaving the army) and volunteered. Work came late, mid-pillar-three ('I'm not sure what you do for work'), but did cover the desk-bound question. No health-conditions question; the herniated disc was volunteered in the prospect's opening answer, though the rep did follow up on it usefully. Training week and diet emerged in fragments during the pitch rather than in baseline. Sleep never touched. 'How do you feel on a day-to-day on a random Tuesday? Paint the picture' is a good question and got the achy/creaky answer, but is not the energy-through-the-day check.

P3.evidence: The best goals work in this batch. Explored function over aesthetics properly ('is it so you can avoid injuries like the herniated disc, or is there any other reason?') which produced the paddle boarding, jiu-jitsu and judo list. Bridged out of the physical — 'has that impacted or affected you in other arenas of your life?' — and got identity. Ran the future-self question ('40-year-old Steven, aside from the six-pack... who do you really want to see back in your eyes, on an identity level?'), then P3f ('who else would benefit by you being more...?') and refused to accept the first thin answer, pushing twice with 'In what way specifically though?' and 'Tell me more', which produced the real driver: 'that's one less thing I have to worry about and more brain power I can give to my family and my work.' Only the explicit reflect-back was substituted with a reframe rather than delivered.

P4.evidence: P4f ran early and well, tailored to the prospect: 'you said you've kind of been in the holistic space for the best part of 15, 17 years... Why would you say you need additional help? Because YouTube, ChatGPT, TikTok, Google, the information is out there. So why does someone with your experience need us?' The root-cause question also landed — 'what do you feel like the biggest culprit is for why it's been half a decade?' — producing self-doubt, overwhelm and social eating. Then the rep overwrote the prospect's own diagnosis with his own label: 'if you were to put that in a word, would you say comfort is the biggest culprit for yourself?' The prospect had said self-doubt; he agreed to 'comfort' because it was offered. That is exactly what P4e says not to do.

P5.evidence: Strongest consequence frame in the batch. 'At the end of the day, my friend, what happens if you don't?' produced 'Things don't change. Or they get worse.' Followed immediately with the settle check — 'And you don't strike me as someone who is willing to accept that?' — and got 'No', which the prospect then reinforced himself with the Walter Reed story and 'I'm not going to be just a broken person for the rest of my life.' Landed the line in the sand: 'So you're actually ready to take that step?' / 'Yeah.' Only the explicit 'why not' was left to the prospect to supply rather than asked.

P6.evidence: P6a ran verbatim and got a strong answer: 'the most important question of the day, do you feel internally capable of actually following step-by-step instructions and being a good student of Trevor?' — 'Yeah. No, I actually struggle a lot with ambiguity. So this seems the opposite of that.' P6b never ran, and this is the decisive miss on the call: 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in on this?' is the question that surfaces a fiancée with veto power. Instead the partner blocker appeared for the first time after the price, which is where it is hardest to work.

P11.evidence: Payment was partially collected — a $100 refundable deposit went through a PayFunnels link and was confirmed live ('Yep, it went through' / 'Yep, I've seen that') — but not programme payment. No Trevor onboarding call was actually scheduled; a Wednesday call with Trevor was described as part of the $1,200 pitch but the only thing booked was a 15-minute follow-up with the rep himself. No agreement email, nothing signed on the call, no welcome email, no Skool link and no onboarding questionnaire, none of which were reachable without a real sale.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete play run anywhere in this batch. Ran: is she on the call and in the house, got her name, checked she was supportive ('is she receptive? Is she supportive of you actually stepping into your higher self?'), the social-proof story about the Oklahoma prospect whose wife joined and signed up, the invitation for Hannah to join and ask questions, the precedent question ('Have you guys made a decision like this before, when it comes to this amount?' — a bathroom remodel) and whose idea that was, the blocker isolate ('what is the main potential that could prevent you from doing this? Is it just the finances?'), and finally the scripted stuck-fallback: deposit now, talk to her, full refund if she says no. NOT run: 'Is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain?', 'Is this genuinely needing her input — or asking permission to bet on yourself?', and 'This isn't a joint decision like buying a house. Is that responsibility hers or yours?' Those three challenge moves were skipped in favour of accommodating the partner, which is a defensible read on a couple who have only just combined finances but is not the script.

The isolate ran — 'So if you guys find a way to make the finances make sense, you're in?' / 'Yeah.' — and correctly established money as the only blocker. Nothing else did. No 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no 'most clients pay upfront but for some we break it up', no permission question, and none of the six financial-picture questions, despite the prospect handing over a precise household threshold ('close to $1,000, it's like, okay, it's going to be a much longer conversation'). The rep answered a $1,000 threshold by inventing a $1,200 product rather than by finding out what the household could actually do.

Script gap worth recording: the prospect's rehabilitation success came from a cheap alternative that genuinely worked — 'I paid $350 for a personal physical therapist... And he helped me and then he introduced me to foundation training.' That is a $350 intervention that solved the problem $6,000 is being asked to solve, and there is no scripted play for it. The rep neither surfaced it as a comparison nor pre-empted it before Hannah could.

notes: Discovery here was genuinely excellent — P3 and P5 both ran close to the intent of the script and the prospect ended the pitch saying 'this is what I needed, really.' The whole call then turned on one missing question: P6b would have surfaced the fiancée before the price rather than after it. Because it did not, the rep had to improvise three separate commercial structures in eight minutes to hold the deal together. Coach P6b, and coach holding the line on price once OB is running — the deposit was scripted, the $1,200 trial and the buyer-chosen deposit amount were not.
